# ataila_catalogue_items (Data Source)

What tenants can order on the platform: every enabled catalogue item, in display order, with its order form, how an order of it counts against the tenant's quotas (`ataila_tenant_quota`), and whether every order of it needs an operator's approval. This is the operator's view; a tenant orders, and sees its price estimate, in the portal. Needs a token holding `orders-read-global` (or `orders-admin-global`) and platform release 1.0.233 or later.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "ataila_catalogue_items" "all" {}

# The order form of the AI gateway key item.
output "ai_key_form" {
  value = jsondecode(one([
    for i in data.ataila_catalogue_items.all.items : i.spec_schema_json if i.key == "ai-gateway-key"
  ]))
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) The enabled items, by `sort_order`, then `key`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `edition` (String) Which platform editions offer it: `sp` (service-provider platforms) or `both`.
- `key` (String) The item's key, for example `ai-gateway-key`.
- `kind` (String) What delivering an order of the item creates: `vdi-desktop`, `project-vm`, `ai-gateway-key`, `project`, `k8s-namespace`, `storage` or `manual` (an operator delivers it by hand).
- `name` (String) Its display name.
- `price_hint_json` (String) As JSON text: which cost units price an order of the item (`unit_keys`); null when the item has no price basis. The EUR estimate itself is the tenant's, in the portal.
- `quota_dimensions_json` (String) As JSON text: how an order's spec maps onto quota dimensions, per dimension `{"const": n}`, `{"field": "<spec field>"}` or `{"field": …, "map": {…}}`.
- `requires_approval` (Boolean) Every order of the item goes to an operator's approval card, whatever the quota says.
- `sort_order` (Number) Display order, ascending.
- `spec_schema_json` (String) The order form as JSON text: a JSON Schema object (`type`, `properties`, `required`, defaults and limits) an order's spec must satisfy. Read it with `jsondecode()`.
